approach: Write the acceleration on the smooth and rough 45° inclines, use the given time ratio to relate them, and solve for the coefficient of kinetic friction.

steps.text: On the smooth 45° incline, the block's acceleration equals the gravity component along the incline, with nothing else acting.
On the rough 45° incline, kinetic friction subtracts from this.
Both blocks start from rest and cover the same incline length L, and time for a fixed distance from rest goes as the inverse square root of the acceleration.
The rough time is twice the smooth time, so squaring this ratio gives the rough acceleration as one quarter of the smooth acceleration.
Substitute and solve for μ at θ = 45°, where sin45° = cos45° so they cancel.
